findings.title: No load-tier test covers the Runner's subprocess/budget tick path
findings.description: The Python rules require "at least one load test exercising a realistic configuration" for "any code on the simulation, network, concurrency, or environment-layer paths," and state CI must gate it, with load tests asserting "latency, throughput, or resource bounds — not just functional correctness." The Runner is squarely a concurrency/environment path: `RunnerTenant.tick` (src/amoeba/runner/tenant.py:96) spawns detached children (`launch.py` `Popen` with `start_new_session`), polls them (`LaunchTracker.reap`), and issues bounded `sq`/`cf` subprocess calls gated by `TickBudget`. I confirmed `tests/load/` contains no Runner test — `test_crash_loop.py` drives `JOURNALING_TENANT`, not `RunnerTenant` — and no load test asserts the bounds this path should hold (start-to-ready under the Runner, per-tick time near `tick_deadline_seconds` + one `tick_call_timeout_seconds`, zombie count under repeated launches). The `tests/runner/` crash harness *does* exercise this machinery with real subprocesses and SIGKILL, so crash-safety is well covered; but it asserts end-state correctness, not resource/latency bounds, and it lives outside `tests/load/`, so a CI gate scoped to that directory would not pick up a Runner regression. Mitigating factor worth stating plainly: slice 122's `PRODUCTION_PLANNERS` is empty, so the "realistic configuration" is minimal this slice, and deferring the load test to 125 (dispatch planner) is defensible — but that deferral should be a recorded decision rather than an accident of where the tests landed.

findings.title: Crash-recovery end states verified against the real store and recovery code
findings.description: The four kill points in `tests/runner/test_crash_recovery.py` rest on behavior that I confirmed in the underlying modules rather than trusting the diff. `BETWEEN_BLOCK_AND_RESOLVE` depends on `finish.record` → `_block_once` (no second block when `store.blocked_state_for` is non-None) followed by `journal_resolve`; `block`'s transaction and `resolve`'s `rowcount != 1` guard (src/amoeba/store/blocking.py, src/amoeba/store/journal.py) make "one block, entry resolved" on re-entry true. `BEFORE_LAUNCH`'s `not_applied` depends on `SquadronRunIdObserver._not_found` returning `NotApplied` once `issued_at + grace` is past (src/amoeba/process/observers/sq_run_id.py), and `WHILE_RUNNING`/`AFTER_FINISH`'s "left for the issuer" depends on `reconcile`'s `InFlight` case leaving the entry unresolved. All four match the store's actual semantics, so the crash proof is sound, not merely self-consistent.

findings.title: The single broad except is a documented, mechanically-pinned process boundary
findings.description:
`except Exception` here is the one place a tenant-internal error would otherwise reach the resident loop. It logs at ERROR via `logger.exception`, does not swallow (it calls `escalate(...)` to name the node/project), and only re-raises store/shape errors explicitly. `tests/runner/test_tenant.py::test_the_runner_package_has_exactly_one_broad_except` enforces count 1 across the package, and `test_a_store_failure_or_shape_error_propagates` confirms the re-raise path. This satisfies the "documented top-level handler at a process boundary" exception to the no-`except Exception` rule.

A minor, non-blocking observation folded in for completeness: `decide.py` defines several related value types (`RunState`, `InFlightRun`, `LaunchRun`, `ProjectView`, `Planner`) plus the `decide` function in one module, and `observe.py` runs 326 lines — both slightly past the one-class-per-file / ~300-line guidance. They are cohesive to a single stage (the D1/D6 seams) and grouped deliberately, so this is "practical" overflow rather than a defect.
